verdict.rationale: The Comptroller's own pages say returns can be filed and paid online through Webfile, which is reached through an authenticated eSystems account, by electronic check or credit card. The core file/pay transaction is therefore online for many taxes. But the same pages say Texas Franchise reports are filed electronically only through approved third-party tax software, and some forms must be downloaded, filled out in Adobe Reader, and printed and mailed. Online completion is therefore not universal across the service's transactions. missing for 10: a first-party online path for every core filing (franchise reports go through third-party software, some forms are paper-only), online new-business registration documented on the Comptroller's pages, and independent or hands-on confirmation of an end-to-end online filing (the probe stopped at the authenticated eSystems front door).

support.subject: As a founder, the core transaction this service exists for (form, register, apply, file, or pay) can be completed online, per the service's own published pages

citations.quote: With Webfile, you can file your return early and post-date the electronic check payment by changing the payment effective date.
